mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses equity valuations by raising discount rates applied to future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has risen over the past month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5% in a 3-month window, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) indicates a supply shock that disrupts the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (INDPRO decline and RSAFS rise) fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 days due to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months), the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) over the past month signals strong consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 in a 3-month average, it indicates a weakening manufacturing sector that reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO below 100 in 3 months fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a severe labor market contraction that reduces household income and consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise) fails to predict negative returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic expansions (when housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1500 thousand units), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 days due to overheating and potential policy tightening.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions (HOUST > 1500), the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
